8734.t: BM4450: Modelling and Simulation in Bioengineering
8734.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM4450 : Modelling and Simulation in Bioengineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1 (6 h)
Introduction
System definition and properties
Signals and systems
Modelling and simulation
Applications in bioengineering
Module 2 (10 h)
Requirements for models (Qualitative and quantitative aspects) aspects of implementation and interface target response data case studies
Conceptual models (Block and component diagrams case studies) Mathematical models (two-physical system based models, state variable models) representation of fluid circuits, gas uptake and distribution, simple transfer in neural systems
Module 3 (10 h)
Aspects related to implementation of models through software platforms (discretization of continuous time-state equation associated algorithms for discretization case studies) simulation and validation of case studies
Module 4 (10 h)
Model of cardio-respiratory system, circulation, respiration, and physiological control, sensitivity analysis

Course Objective

1 .

To provide an understanding of systems, signals, and their relevance in bioengineering applications.
2 .

To develop skills for creating and analyzing mathematical and conceptual models in bioengineering.
3 .

To equip students with the ability to implement and simulate bioengineering models using software platforms.
4 .

To foster the ability to analyze physiological systems and perform sensitivity analyses of models.

Course Outcome

1 .

Students will be able to:
1. Define systems and signals and explain their properties in the context of bioengineering.
2. Design and interpret qualitative and quantitative models for bioengineering applications, including conceptual and mathematical approaches.
3. Implement and simulate mathematical models using computational tools and evaluate their accuracy.
4. Develop and validate models of physiological systems such as cardio-respiratory and neural systems.
5. Perform sensitivity analysis on models to assess system behavior under varying conditions.

Essential Reading

1 .

William Van Meurs, Modeling and Simulation in Biomedical Engineering: Applications in Cardiorespiratory Physiology, Mc Graw Hill , 1st Edition

2 .

Nenad Filipovic, Computational Modeling and Simulation Examples in Bioengineering, IEEE Press , 1st Edition

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Yie Siew Choong, Computational Modelling and Simulation in Biomedical Research, Bentham Books , ISBN: 978-981-5165-47-0 (Print)

2 .

Rogier P. Wijk van Brievingh, Dietmar P. F. Möller, Biomedical Modeling and Simulation on a PC, Springer Verlag , Volume 6

6942.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE3704 : Structural Engineering Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Experiement 1: [3 hrs]
Tests on cement: (a) Determination of consistency of standard cement paste as per Indian Standard IS 4031: Part 4: 1988, (b) Determination of initial and final setting times as per IS 4031: Part 5: 1988, and (c) Determination of soundness of cement as per IS 4031: Part 3: 1988
Experiement 2: [3 hrs]
Tests on fine aggregates: (a) Determination of particle size and shape as per IS 2386: Part I: 1963 and (b) Determination of specific gravity and water absorption as per IS 2386: Part III: 1963
Experiement 3: [3 hrs]
Tests on coarse aggregates: (a) Determination of particle size and shape as per IS 2386: Part I: 1963 and (b) Determination of specific gravity and water absorption as per IS 2386: Part III: 1963
Experiement 4: [3 hrs]
Test on bricks: (a) compressive strength as per IS 3495: Part 1: 2019 and (b) water absorption as per IS 3495: Part 2: 2019
Experiement 5: [3 hrs]
Test on high strength deformed steel reinforcement bars: (a) tensile test as per IS 1786: 2008
Experiement 6: [3 hrs]
Concrete mix proportioning as per IS 10262: 2019
Experiement 7: [3 hrs]
Test on hardened concrete: (a) compressive strength, flexural strength and split tensile strength as per IS 516: 2021
Experiement 8: [3 hrs]
Non-destructive testing of concrete: (a) using ultrasonic pulse velocity as per IS 516: Part 5: Sec 1: 2018 and (b) using rebound hammer as per IS 13311 (Part-1):1992 (IS 516: Part 5: Sec 4: 2020)
Experiement 9: [3 hrs]
Test on RC Beams deficient in flexure
Experiement 10: [3 hrs]
Test on RC Beams deficient in shear

Course Objective

1 .

To learn the properties of cement, aggregates, bricks, and reinforcing steel bars
2 .

To learn the properties of fresh and harden concrete
3 .

To learn the failure patterns of scaled model of RC beams
4 .

To learn the properties of harden concrete by performing the non-destructive tests.

Course Outcome

1 .

Students will be able to
1. find the properties of cement, aggregates, bricks, and reinforcing steel bars by conducting laboratory tests according to relevant Indian standards.
2. find properties of fresh concrete by conducting tests according to Indian Standard.
3. find the compressive strength of 7 days, 14 days and 28 days harden concrete by loading it to failure
4. to perform laboratory tests on scaled structural models.
5. perform non-destructive tests on harden concrete to estimate its strength

8222.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MM1701 : Introduction to Materials Engineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Syllabus for MM1701 (Introduction to Materials Engineering)
Introductions: Classes of Materials Metals and Alloys, Ceramics, Polymers, Composite Materials, Advanced Materials.
Crystal Structure: Single Crystals, Polycrystalline materials, Unit Cells, Point Coordinates, Crystallographic Directions, Crystallographic Planes, Family of Planes.
Structure of Materials: Bohr Atomic Models, Materials DNA, Types of Bonding.
Thermodynamics of Metal extraction: Internal Energy, Enthalpy, Entropy, Free Energy, Single Component System, Clausius-Clapeyron equation, Ideal Solution, Regular Solution, Concept of solid solution, Ellingham Diagram, Importance and application of Ellingham diagram.
Principles of Metal extraction: Introduction, Steps for Metal Extraction, Process of Metal Extraction, Pyrometallurgy Calcination, Roasting, Smelting, Refining, BF-BOF Route, Hydrometallurgy, Electrometallurgy.
Mechanical Behavior of Materials: Tensile Testing, Engineering Stress-strain Curve, Strain Hardening, Anelastic Behavior, Bauschinger effect, True Stress-strain curve, Compression Testing, Shear Testing, Torsion, Hardness testing, Macrohardness and Microhardness, Brinell hardness, Rockwell Hardness, Vickers macro and microhardness, Knoop microhardness.
Fracture behavior of materials: Theoretical Cohesive Strength, Griffith theory of fracture mechanics, Process of fracture, Types of fracture, Ductile fracture, Brittle fracture, Fractographic aspect of ductile and brittle fracture, Stress Concentration, Fracture Mechanics: Strain Energy Release Rate, Stress Intensity Factor, Fracture Toughness, Modes of Failure.
Defect Theory: Theoretical Shear Strength, Types of Defects, Point Defects, Line Defects (Dislocations) Edge Dislocations, Climb of Dislocations, Screw Dislocations, Dislocation Loops, Cross slip of dislocations, Observation of dislocations, Pile up of dislocations, Sources of dislocations, Interfacial defects, Volume defects.
Dislocation Theory and Strengthening Mechanism: Slip System, Slip in single crystal, Slip in polycrystalline material, Deformation by twinning, Strengthening Mechanism, Solid Solution Strengthening, Grain Boundary Strengthening, Precipitation Strengthening, Cold Working, Stored Energy, Effect of heat treatment on cold worked structure, Recovery, Recrystallization, Grain Growth.
Phase Transformation: Introduction, Solid Solution, Hume-Rothery Law, Microstructures, Phase Diagrams, Purpose of Phase Diagrams, Gibbs Phase Rule, Single and Two Component System, Binary isomorphous systems, Tie-Line Rule, Lever Rule, Binary Eutectic Systems, Equilibrium Cooling, Non-Equilibrium Cooling, Free-energy composition diagram, Iron-Carbon Phase Diagram.
Characterization: Introduction, Techniques of Characterization, Scanning Electron Microscope, Transmission Electron Microscope.

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the different classes of materials, and have a fundamental idea about the crystal structure.
2 .

To provide a basic understanding of materials engineering comprising of the extraction, processing, microstructure, and mechanical properties of the materials.
3 .

To learn about the thermodynamic principles responsible for the metal extraction process and also explore the different types of extraction process.
4 .

To analyze the mechanical and fracture behavior of materials and understand the effect of microstructures such as phases, defects etc. and various strengthening mechanism on the overall structure-property relationship. Apart from the mechanical properties, the unersatnding associated with the electrochemical and corrosion behavior of metals and alloys are needed to be understood.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Upon successful completion, students will be able to gather knowledge about different classes of materials and explore their atomic structure including the crystal structure, unit cells and crystallographic orientation.
2. The course will not only provide an understanding of the thermodynamic concepts for the metal extraction process, but also be able to describe the principles and steps involved in various metal extraction processes.
3. The course will provide insights into the mechanical and fracture behavior of materials and also decipher the underlying mechanics responsible for failure.
4. The course addresses the role of defects (points, line, interfacial, volume) and various strengthening mechanism in materials, helping student in understanding their impact on mechanical properties.
5. The students will realize the importance of phases and phase transformation in metal and alloys.
6. This course also delves into the understanding of various characterization techniques, specifically Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) etc. to examine material structures.

Essential Reading

1 .

William D. Callister, Jr., David G. Rethwisch, Material Science and Engineering, Wiley

2 .

William F. Smith, Javad Hashemi, Foundations of Materials Science and Engineering, McGraw Hill

Supplementary Reading

1 .

David A. Porter, Kenneth E. Easterling, Mohamed Y Sherif, Phase Transformations in Metals and Alloys, CRC Press

2 .

George E. Dieter, Mechanical Metallurgy, McGraw Hill

Journal and Conferences

1 .

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CY4316 : Computational Chemistry { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Concept of molecular modeling: coordinate systems, potential energy surface, mathematical concept. An introduction to computational quantum mechanics: molecular orbital calculations, Hartree-Fock equations, basis sets, semi-empirical methods, concept of density functional theory. Molecular mechanics: potential energy functional forms, force-field models and parametrization process. Energy minimization methods to explore the energy surface. Computer simulation methods: phase space, practical aspects of computer simulations, tracating potential and minimum image convention. Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulation methos. Conformational analysis: simulated annealing, clustering algorithms. Use of molecular modeling: molecular descriptors, molecular docking, quantitative structure-activity relationships.

Course Objective

1 .

The course aims to discuss the use of sets of theories and techniques for investigating chemical problems on computer and interprets the results with the experimental data.
2 .

To understand the dynamics of structural transitions.
3 .

Student will learn modelling of molecular structures.
4 .

To enhance capability to build careers in academia and industry of molecular modelling.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1:The course aims to discuss the use of sets of theories and techniques for investigating chemical problems on computer and interprets the results with the experimental data.
CO2: It provides basic understanding and importance on Electronic structure models for the prediction of energies, thermodynamic quantities, geometries, and electronic and spectral properties.
CO3: It provides the knowledge on Empirical force field models and their use in chemical and biochemical studies.
CO4: It would help students to understand the strengths and limitations of each technique.
CO5:This would help students to link between theory and experiments. The course further demonstrates a working knowledge of a range of computational chemistry packages.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EE4703 : Communication Systems Laboratory { 0-0-2 / 1}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

1. Observation the operation of different modules of ETT-101 Telecoms Trainer kit and modelling equations by using those modules.
2. Setting of an Amplitude modulator and demodulator by using ETT-101 telecom trainer kit and measurement of its depth of modulation.
3. Setting of a DSB-SC modulator and demodulator by using ETT-101 telecom trainer kit and analysis of the effect of signal parameters on transmitted and received signal.
4. Setting of a SSB-SC modulator and demodulator by using ETT-101 telecom trainer kit and analysis of the effect of signal parameters on transmitted and received signal.
5. Setting of a Frequency modulator and demodulator by using ETT-101 telecom trainer kit and analysis of the effect of signal parameters on transmitted and received signal.
6. Observation of the operation different sampling techniques on message signal and examine the effect of aliasing.
7. Analysis of the transmission and reception of a speech signal in PAM/TDM system.
8. Setting of a pulse width modulator and demodulator by using ETT-101 telecom trainer kit and observe its operation for message signal, speech signal.
9. Setting of PCM encoder and decoder by using ETT-101 telecom trainer kit and measuring the SNDR of the signal on the PCM decoder’s output.
10. Implementation of Delta Modulation and demodulation techniques by using ETT-101 telecom trainer kit and observation of the integrator’s step size on the delta modulator’s slope overload and granularity characteristics.
11. Implementation of Delta-sigma Modulation and demodulation techniques by using ETT-101 telecom trainer kit.
12. Mini Projects relevant to the experiments.

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the analog communication system and representation of signals.
2 .

To comprehend various analog modulation & demodulation schemes, their design, operation & applications.
3 .

To understand the sampling, pulse modulation schemes, multiplexing techniques.
4 .

To understand the PCM encoding and decoding, delta modulation, and delta-sigma modulation

Course Outcome

1 .

Understand the concepts of analog and digital communication and be familiar with hardware components (Emona kit and various discrete components).
2 .

Design an amplitude modulation (canonical AM, DSB-SC, SSB) system using the Emona kit.

3 .

Design FM generation and detection using Emona kit.

4 .

Design sampling and reconstruction processes, time division multiplexing, pulse modulation & Demodulation, and transmission & reception of a speech signal using Emona kit.
5 .

Design PCM encoding and decoding, delta modulation, and delta-sigma modulation using Emona kit.

8478.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MM4261 : Joining of Metals Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Principle, Theory and Classification of welding and other joining processes. Manual metal arc (MMA): Equipment requirement, electrodes for welding of structural steels, coating constituents and their functions, types of coatings, current and voltage selection for electrodes, Arc welding power sources Conventional welding transformers, rectifiers and current and voltage. The influence of these power sources on welding. Metal transfer. Submerged arc welding (SAW): Process details, consumables such as fluxes and wires for welding mild steel, Variations in submerged arc welding process. Gas metal arc welding (GMAW) or MIG/ MAG welding: Process details, shielding gases, electrode wires, their sizes, and welding current ranges. TIG welding: Process details, power sources requirements, electrode sizes and materials, current carrying capacities of different electrodes, shielding gases, application of process. Resistance welding: General principle of heat generation in resistance welding, application of resistance welding processes. Process details and working principle of spot, seam, and. projection welding, electrode materials, shapes of electrodes, electrode cooling, selection of welding currents, voltages. Welding metallurgy of carbon and alloy steels, Cast irons, Stainless steels, Al- and Cu-based alloys.Weldability and Heat affected zones (HAZ). Welding defects and detection techniques. Soldering and brazing: Difference between both the processes, consumables used, methods of brazing, fluxes used, their purposes and flux residue treatment.

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the principle of metal joining or non-metal joining.
2 .

To get acquainted with different welding techniques and designs in detail.
3 .

To compare and contrast welding, brazing, and soldering processes.
4 .

To understand weldability, HAZ zones, welding stresses, and welding defects.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. The course integrates the principles and practices of different welding, brazing, and soldering processes to understand the metallurgy of joining.
2. Joint preparation and its importance for quality joining are discussed.
3. Different types of joining like welding, brazing, soldering, and riveting are presented to compare and contrast amongst these.
4. Types of different welding techniques are well demonstrated.
5. Importance of advanced welding techniques is elucidated.
6. Comparison of different welding techniques are presented.

Essential Reading

1 .

J F Lancaster, Metallurgy of Welding, Allen

2 .

R L Little, Welding and Welding Technology, TMH

Supplementary Reading

1 .

J. Norrish, Advanced Welding Processes, Woodhead

2 .

K Weman, Welding Processes Handbook, Wiidhead

5918.t: ME6205: Metal Cutting and Tool Design
5918.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ME6205 : Metal Cutting and Tool Design { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I [Hours 9]
Theory of metal Cutting, Systems of tool nomenclature, machine reference system and tool reference system and its conversion, Geometry of single point cutting tool, orthogonal cutting and oblique cutting, Pissipanen’s card analogy model, Dynamic shear strain, Dynamic shear stress, Force relationship, velocity relationship, Merchant’s Force equilibrium diagram. Derivation of MRS system of Tool geometry to ORS and NRS System, Derivation of True Rake angle, Grinding of cutting tool in a cutting tool grinder
Module II [Hours 6 ]
Merchant and Ernst theory, Modified Merchant theory, Lee and Shaffer theory, Introduction to Kudo and Dewhurst theory for machining with chip-curl, Parallel Shear Zone theory, Stress distribution at the chip/tool interface
Module III [Hours 6]
Geometry of drill bit, drilling forces, drilling torque and thrust, Geometry of milling cutter, milling forces, milling torque, feed force and vertical force.
Module IV [Hours 6]
Modes of cutting tool failure, Tool wear, Taylor’s tool life equation, Tool life test, effect of variables on tool life, machinability criteria, theory and application of cutting fluid, Economics of machining, Minimum cost per piece, Maximum production rate, Maximum profit rate
Module V [Hours 9]
Design of single point cutting tool, Design of flat and circular form tool, Design of broach, Design of high production cutting tool with controlled contact, Types of chip-breaker, underbreaking and over-breaking limit, Hot-machining and cryo-machining, Explosive machining, PVD and CVD coated tool, cryo-treated tool

Course Objective

1 .

To enhance the fundamental knowledge in metal cutting theory
2 .

Able to apply theory to practical problems
3 .

Able to apply theory to design of cutting tool
4 .

Able to determine economic tool life of cutting tools

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: Able to design cutting tool using metal cutting theory
CO2: This will help to design different cutting tools
CO3:This will help to analyse multipoint cutting tools
CO4. This will help to determine economic tool life of cutting tool
CO5. Knwoledge of machinability criteria will be enhanced
